name: Dames Vertes

attributes.attribute: lure travelers into ravines and over waterfalls
travel on the wind and make plants grow
dress always in green in human form

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Dames Vertes are French folkloric figures, the Green Ladies. They lurk in the forests of parts of France that were once Celtic territory. They draw travelers into ravines with their beauty and sweet voices. They torment their victims by holding them upside down over waterfalls and laughing at their terror. They travel across the land on the wind, and their breath makes plants grow. Such elemental spirits appear in many cultures. In the case of the Dames Vertes, the wind is their chief carrier. They can take human form, and when they do they dress always in green. Green is a color known in Ireland as the favorite choice of the fairy people. They belong to the same family as the Green Ladies of Britain.
objective: Document the Dames Vertes, the Green Ladies of French folklore.
key_results: Record the Dames Vertes as forest spirits who lure travelers into ravines.
Document their habit of holding victims over waterfalls.
Note their travel on the wind and their green clothing.
Link them to the British Green Ladies.
